article.title: Calibration vs. Ranking: Two Different Ways a Model Can Be Good
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Two predictive models can both be useful while being good in different ways. Ranking asks whether the model places higher-risk or higher-propensity cases above lower ones. Calibration asks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies. A model can rank customers extremely well but be poorly calibrated. Suppose customers scored at 0.80 convert only 40 percent of the time, while customers scored at 0.20 convert 10 percent of the time. The ordering may still be excellent even though the probabilities are too high. For a campaign that simply contacts the top 100,000 customers, ranking may be the main requirement. Metrics such as AUC or lift can help evaluate that use. But if the business calculates expected profit by multiplying a predicted probability by customer value, inaccurate probabilities can produce bad decisions. Calibration then matters directly. Reliability plots, calibration curves, and metrics such as the Brier score can help assess probability quality. Calibration can also change over time when the base rate shifts. A model trained during a high-conversion period may continue to rank customers well while systematically overpredicting probabilities in a weaker market. Recalibration may be sufficient in some cases; full retraining is not always necessary. Analysts should therefore start with the decision. Does the organization need an ordering, a probability estimate, or both? Fraud investigation with fixed review capacity may emphasize ranking near the operational cutoff. Credit risk pricing or expected-loss estimation requires probabilities with meaningful numerical interpretation. Marketing expected-value calculations may need both ranking and calibration, and possibly treatment-effect estimates as well. Saying that a model has “high accuracy” hides these distinctions. A stronger statement is, “The model separates high- and low-risk cases well, but its probability estimates require recalibration.” Model quality is multidimensional. The right metric depends on how predictions are converted into actions. Analysts should define the population, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed pattern from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文重點在於把 model metric 或 KPI 放回實際 decision context。數字變大不一定更好；極端群體可能自然回歸平均；ranking 與 probability calibration 是不同能力；歷史資料也會承載舊政策；而 campaign 真正關心的常常是 intervention 所創造的增量效果。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：model metricやKPIはdecision contextの中で解釈する必要がある。数値が大きいこと自体が良いとは限らず、極端群は平均へ回帰し、rankingとprobability calibrationは別の性能である。historical dataには旧policyも刻まれ、campaignではinterventionによる増分効果が重要になる。
